scores.evidence: none (minor point 6 about the omitted reference list and 'balanced, up-to-date citation of the key adjuvant EGFR-TKI trials' is a general citation request and does not state that the introduction/rationale is inadequate or that justification for the study/3-year duration is missing)

"This is predictable alternation, not a clearly random sequence with allocation concealment. If this is the actual method used, it is a major threat to internal validity and selection bias... I do not think the trial can be considered adequately randomized."

"Please also explain why 141 patients were randomized despite a planned sample size of 124, and whether the power calculation was updated after the protocol amendment." (asks a related question about the power calculation without stating that no sample size/power calculation is reported; mostly over-enrollment criticism, which the key lists as not enough)
"The quality-of-life instrument was developed by the investigators for this trial; please provide evidence of validation and explain the basis for the ≥6-point decline threshold."

"DFS and OS were analyzed in the per-protocol set, not the full randomized population... In a randomized phase 3 trial, an intention-to-treat analysis should be presented as the primary or at least a key sensitivity analysis... This raises concern about informative censoring and bias."

"follow-up was incomplete for a substantial proportion of the PPS ('the remaining 41 patients stopped attending scheduled imaging assessments before any recurrence was documented')... This raises concern about informative censoring and bias." and "the reported follow-up differs between groups and the censoring pattern is substantial."

"The trial did not show an OS benefit (HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.39–1.81; p = 0.65)... statements that icotinib 'should replace osimertinib' and that this applies 'worldwide, including those with stage IB disease, non-Asian patients...' are not justified by the study... should be rewritten to say that 3-year adjuvant icotinib improved DFS in the studied population, not that it prolongs survival or should replace osimertinib globally."

"The abstract reports the primary DFS result as HR 0.40 (95% CI 0.24–0.66; p < 0.001), whereas the Results section reports HR 0.50 (95% CI 0.30–0.82; p = 0.0061) for the same endpoint and population."

"The Results section says '147 patients were enrolled and randomly assigned,' but the treatment groups total 141 (68 + 73). This arithmetic error must be corrected... In the safety text, placebo TEAEs are reported as 22/96 rather than 22/69."
"Nineteen randomized patients were excluded from the efficacy analysis (141 randomized vs 122 in the PPS)... with clear reasons for exclusion from the PPS by arm."
"'The 3-year DFS rate was lower in the icotinib group than in the placebo group...' This sentence is reversed; the numbers show the opposite."
